newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 14.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet stepped back from the coalition's original intention to completely deregulate rents in districts with up to 10,000 residents from next year. Rents in these districts will increase by 27 percent from July 1 this year and will have a slower increase next year.

- The compulsory administrator of Agrobanka says the bank will probably be divided into a healthy part, which will be bought by a strategic investor, while the losses will stay with the remainder of the company.

- The Trade Ministry proposes that energy and gas prices increase on July 1 this year by 18 percent. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik insists that they should increase by 15 or at most 16 percent, which is the same as last year's increase.

- Pro Win, which owns 54 percent of Poldi Steel, has a plan to save the bankrupt steel company. The plan is to cancel the bankruptcy process from the side of the creditors and liquidate the subsidiaries Poldi Konstrukcni and Huti-Uslechtile.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Although Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy says that a definite decision has yet to be made, it is apparent after a meeting of ministers yesterday that Norwegian Statoil will supply from one to three billion square metres of natural gas yearly to the Czech Republic.

- The tempo of growth of money supply in the Czech economy, which has decreased intensely since last May, fell to a record low last December of 9.2 percent, according to Martin Svehla of the Czech National Bank.
- Direct foreign investments in Czech businesses amounted to $1.4 billion last year, according to reports from the Czech National Bank.

- Skoda Plzen is beginning work together with the Swiss munitions company Oerlikon-Contraves, Tatra Koprivnice and Retia Pardubice on a detection system for aircraft. Skoda does not only want to deal with the Czech Army, but would rather like to export the system.
PRAVO - The state's top prosecutor, Bohumira Kopecna, met with Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and requested approval of her resignation by April 1.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus will meet with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn and the chairman of parliament Zoltan Gal on Monday in Budapest.

- Agricultural businesses do not agree with any kind of budget cuts which would affect agriculture, accordiing to the chairman of the Czech-Moravian federation of agricultural businesses, Jaroslav Brom.
- Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy referred to export difficulties as one of the main reasons for the decrease in industrial output in January of this year by 3.9 percent compared to January of 1996.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Health Minister Jan Strasky promised that his secretary Miroslav Macek would present the third version of a concept for health reforms to the cabinet by this evening at the latest.
